Submit - This document contains an excerpt from acts of an epicrisis concerning the son of a certain Julia Sarapias; it dates to 173. The edition records among the witnesses (γνωστῆρες) a man named Julius Marius Tiberinus ([Ἰ]ούλ̣ι̣ο̣ν | Μάριον Τιβ[ερ]εῖνον) (ll. 12–13). The reading ([Ἰ]ούλ̣ι̣ο̣ν is problematic: the purported lambda is very different from any other in the papyrus and highly unusual in its own right. The better reading is Μ̣άρκον. At first glance, kappa seems surprising for the pyramid-shaped letter after rho, but it is perfectly consistent with other examples of the letter in the papyrus—for example, that in ἐκ two lines earlier, which differs from ρκ only by the mid-letter ligature caused by the higher connection with epsilon than with rho. Thus, we should understand the name Marcus Marius Tiberinus. This same person is attested in a legal document from Alexandria (an opening of a will) written thirteen years letter, in 186 (BGU 13.2244.11).
Submit - Name restoration based on image and bibliography.

Commit - The name in l. 15 is Baburius Lucullinus, conjectured in H. Devijver, ZPE 59 (1985) 221, S. Demougin, CahGlotz 18 (2007), 90, all based on S. Daris, Aegyptus 63 (1983) 126-127. However, Daris doesn't appear to restore the name, he prints Bab.rius Lucullinus. It is clear that the papyrus does not have space for more than one letter if one adds the right part of the beta and the left part of the upsilon.
